newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia Suharto says soybean plantations needed.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia Suharto says soybean plantations needed.

text.p: Indonesia's President Suharto said soybean plantations are needed to meet domestic demand of 600,000 tonnes a year, the Suara Pembaruan afternoon newspaper reported on Monday.
He was quoted as saying Indonesia, the world's fourth most populous nation with nearly 200 million people, was continuing to import soybeans.
"We must do it. We must plant ... open soybean plantations," Suharto was quoted as telling reporters returning with him from the World Food Summit in Rome.
He said farmers seemed to be less enthusiastic about growing soybean and corn compared to rice. Industry sources said farmers preferred cultivating rice because of comparatively better prices.
Suharto said Indonesia needed to import 600,000 tonnes of soybeans a year even though there was plenty of land in the archipelago to plant the crop.
"If one hectare (2.5 acres) can produce two tonnes of soybean, we need 300,000 hectares (750,000 acres) of land," he said.
